description: Antimony is a chemical element with the symbol Sb and atomic number 51. It is a lustrous grey metal or metalloid that occurs in nature mainly as the sulfide mineral stibnite (Sb2S3). A silvery, lustrous gray solid that is stable in air at room temperature, it is a member of group 15 of the periodic table.
uses: Antimony compounds have been known since ancient history and were powdered for use as cosmetics (kohl) and medicine. The most common applications for metallic antimony are in alloys with lead and tin for solders, bullets, and plain bearings, and it improves the rigidity of lead-alloy plates in lead-acid batteries. Antimony trioxide is used as an additive for halogen-containing flame retardants, and antimony is used as a dopant in semiconductor devices.
characteristics: Antimony has an electronegativity of 2.05 and a Mohs scale hardness of 3. It is a silvery, lustrous gray solid with a high density of 6.697 g/cm³, but exhibits low hardness and brittleness due to weak bonding between its layers. When heated, it reacts with oxygen to produce antimony trioxide, and it is attacked by oxidizing acids.
